tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the

entries.name: EnterPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task. Getting user sign-off on your approach before writing code prevents wasted effort and ensures alignment. This tool transitions you into plan mode where you can explore the codebase and design an implementation approach for user approval.

## When to Use This Tool

**Prefer using EnterPlanMode** for implementation tasks unless they're simple. Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. **New Feature Implementation**: Adding meaningful new functionality
   - Example: "Add a logout button" - where should it go? What should happen on click?
   - Example: "Add form validation" - what rules? What error messages?

2. **Multiple Valid Approaches**: The task can be solved in several different ways
   - Example: "Add caching to the API" - could use Redis, in-memory, file-based, etc.
   - Example: "Improve performance" - many optimization strategies possible

3. **Code Modifications**: Changes that affect existing behavior or structure
   - Example: "Update the login flow" - what exactly should change?
   - Example: "Refactor this component" - what's the target architecture?

4. **Architectural Decisions**: The task requires choosing between patterns or technologies
   - Example: "Add real-time updates" - WebSockets vs SSE vs polling
   - Example: "Implement state management" - Redux vs Context vs custom solution

5. **Multi-File Changes**: The task will likely touch more than 2-3 files
   - Example: "Refactor the authentication system"
   - Example: "Add a new API endpoint with tests"

6. **Unclear Requirements**: You need to explore before understanding the full scope
   - Example: "Make the app faster" - need to profile and identify bottlenecks
   - Example: "Fix the bug in checkout" - need to investigate root cause

7. **User Preferences Matter**: The implementation could reasonably go multiple ways
   - If you would use AskUserQuestion to clarify the approach, use EnterPlanMode instead
   - Plan mode lets you explore first, then present options with context

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Only skip EnterPlanMode for simple tasks:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- Adding a single function with clear requirements
- Tasks where the user has given very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks (use the Agent tool instead)

## What Happens in Plan Mode

In plan mode, you'll:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase using `find`/Glob, `grep`/Grep, and Read
2. Understand existing patterns and architecture
3. Design an implementation approach
4. Present your plan to the user for approval
5. Use AskUserQuestion if you need to clarify approaches
6. Exit plan mode with ExitPlanMode when ready to implement

## Examples

### GOOD - Use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Add user authentication to the app"
- Requires architectural decisions (session vs JWT, where to store tokens, middleware structure)

User: "Optimize the database queries"
- Multiple approaches possible, need to profile first, significant impact

User: "Implement dark mode"
- Architectural decision on theme system, affects many components

User: "Add a delete button to the user profile"
- Seems simple but involves: where to place it, confirmation dialog, API call, error handling, state updates

User: "Update the error handling in the API"
- Affects multiple files, user should approve the approach

### BAD - Don't use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Fix the typo in the README"
- Straightforward, no planning needed

User: "Add a console.log to debug this function"
- Simple, obvious implementation

User: "What files handle routing?"
- Research task, not implementation planning

## Important Notes

- This tool REQUIRES user approval - they must consent to entering plan mode
- If unsure whether to use it, err on the side of planning - it's better to get alignment upfront than to redo work
- Users appreciate being consulted before significant changes are made to their codebase

entries.name: ExitPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

name: alloq-implementation
description: Alloq house rules for writing code in this repo - architecture map, layer placement, handler authorization contract, German UI text, test recipes and the definition of done. Load this before writing or changing any code in the Alloq repo, for every implementation task - add a feature, fix a bug, refactor, add a field, entity, page, state, handler, service or component, write an Alembic migration, or add tests - even when the request looks small or does not mention architecture. Use it alongside the generic skills (python-coding, python-clean-code, reflex-state-and-architecture, reflex-testing-state, appkit-commons, appkit-mantine-reference); this skill says how Alloq applies them.

# Alloq implementation

Alloq is a Reflex 0.10 app for resource and project planning. The generic skills
explain Python, Reflex and appkit in general. This skill is the Alloq layer: where
code goes in this repo, which guards it must keep green, and how Alloq tests look.
When the two disagree, this skill wins, because it describes the code as it is.

Stack: Python 3.14, uv workspace (`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv.mac`), Reflex 0.10,
appkit-* (`appkit_mantine as mn`, `appkit_commons`, `appkit_user`, `appkit_ui`),
SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, Pydantic, Alembic, PostgreSQL in production and SQLite in tests.
UI text is German. Code, comments and log messages are English.

## Workflow for every task

1. **Search memory** for the feature words and for error text you see. Past sessions
   stored traps here (for example the mixin rule and the umlaut escaping in tests).
2. **Read the reference code of the layer you touch** before writing. The canonical
   slice is departments (see the architecture map). Copying its shape is faster and
   keeps reviews short.
3. **Plan the smallest diff.** Change the layers the task needs and nothing else. Do
   not move files, rename folders or refactor neighbours unless asked.
4. **Write or adjust the test first**, in the test file of the package you change.
   For a bug, first write a test that fails because of the bug. Run the touched test
   files once before changing code, so you know which failures were already there;
   report those instead of fixing them inside the same diff.
5. **Implement.**
6. **Run the gates**: `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test`.
   For a quick loop run only the touched test files with
   `uv run pytest <file> -q`, but run `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` whenever
   you add or change an event handler.
7. **Check file sizes**: `python .claude/skills/alloq-implementation/scripts/check_file_sizes.py`.
8. **Update memory** with any new trap or decision that the code itself does not show.

## Architecture map

Host app `app/` (entry `app/app.py`, admin pages `app/pages/*.py`, sidebar in
`app/components/sidebar.py`) plus uv workspace packages in `components/`:

| Package | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `alloq-commons` | shared kernel: entities, models, repositories, shared services, shared UI, `theme.py`, `roles.py`, `access.py` |
| `alloq-project` | projects and planning: `components/`, `services/`, `states/`, `pages.py` |
| `alloq-dashboard` | dashboard and portfolio: same layout, `models.py` for card payloads |
| `alloq-team` | team overview and employees: same layout |

Layers, in the order data flows (paths for departments under
`components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/`):

| Layer | Where | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entity | `entities/department.py` | `class XEntity(Entity, Base)`, `to_dict()` with every field |
| Model | `models/department.py` | Pydantic read model plus `XCreate` write model with `Field` limits |
| Repository | `repositories/department_repository.py` | `BaseRepository[XEntity, AsyncSession]`, `model_class`, module singleton `x_repo` |
| Service | `<pkg>/services/*.py` | pure functions and dataclasses; DB loading kept in `*_inputs.py` or loader functions |
| State | `state/department_states.py` | `rx.State`, `rx.Field` vars, `@rx.event` handlers |
| Component | `components/department.py` | plain functions returning `rx.Component`, built from `mn.*` and shared parts |
| Page | `app/pages/departments.py` or `<pkg>/pages.py` | page factory `create_x_page(sidebar, route, title)` using `app_page` |
| Registration | `app/app.py` | call the factory with `sidebar()`; add a sidebar entry if needed |
| Migration | `alembic/versions/YYYY_MM_DD_<topic>.py` | hand-written, real `downgrade()` |

Dependency direction: feature packages import `alloq_commons` and appkit, never
`app` (`tests/test_component_boundaries.py` fails otherwise). Feature packages do not
import each other unless that import already exists. `app` may import everything.

`alloq_commons` has both `state/` (departments, roles) and `states/` (holidays). Put
new code next to its closest neighbour and do not merge the folders unasked.

Details, snippets and the background-load pattern: `references/architecture.md`.

## Where does this code belong?

- **Pure calculation** (scores, sums, sorting, grouping, labels) goes into a service
  function or a small dataclass, testable without a database. Examples:
  `alloq_dashboard/services/resource_path.py`, `alloq_project/services/project_sorting.py`.
- **Database reads and writes** go through a repository method, or a loader function
  such as `load_departments()` or `portfolio_inputs.py`. States do not build SQL.
- **UI state** (open dialogs, filters, toggles, selection) lives in the state. When the
  state file is large, put new vars and handlers into a mixin
  (`class XListState(rx.State, mixin=True)`), never into a substate; substates break
  tests that create the state on its own.
- **Rendering** goes into function components that read state vars. No logic beyond
  `rx.cond` / `rx.foreach` and formatting.
- **A value both the UI and a test need** (labels, messages, column lists) becomes a
  module constant, so tests can assert on it.

## Security: the handler authorization contract

Access levels (`alloq_commons.access`): admins may do everything; the project
manager role may read and edit every planning page (dashboard, planning, projects,
team) but not the administration; the employee role may only read planning and
projects. Page guards (`admin_only=True`, `editor_only`, `viewer_only`) only hide
the page. Event handlers run over the websocket for anyone with a session, so every
handler protects itself. `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` enforces this for all
states in the four packages. For each new or changed handler pick exactly one case:

1. **Reads or writes data in a planning package** (`alloq_dashboard`,
   `alloq_project`, `alloq_team`, `SidebarState`) → `@rx.event` then
   `@requires_editor` from `alloq_commons.access`. This is the default; the guard
   test rejects `@requires_admin` there.
1b. **Administration state** (`DepartmentState`, `RoleState`, `HolidayState`,
   `DatabaseAccessState`, listed in `ADMIN_STATES`) → `@requires_admin` from
   `appkit_user.authentication.decorators`.
2. **Read-only load the employee role may also run** → `@requires_viewer` from
   `alloq_commons.access`, and add the name to `VIEWER_HANDLERS`. It must not write.
3. **Only changes UI state** (open/close, set filter, toggle) → no decorator, add the
   name to `UI_ONLY_HANDLERS["<ConcreteState>"]`. The test scans its source and the
   `self.` helpers it calls for DB markers (`get_asyncdb_session`, `_repo.`,
   `aggregation.`, ...), so a UI-only handler must not touch a repository or session.
4. **Background handler** (`@rx.event(background=True)`) → guard decorators are not
   allowed (they need the state lock). Check edit rights inside `async with self`
   through `_CardLoadMixin._run_card_load` (`_can_edit`) and list it in
   `INLINE_ADMIN_CHECK`.

Edit controls in the planning UI go inside `editor_only(...)` or use
`disabled=~CAN_EDIT`; `admin_only(...)` is for administration only.

Handlers defined in a mixin are listed under the concrete state that mixes it in
(`TeamState`, `ProjectState`, `PlanningStore`), because the test skips mixins.
Remove allowlist entries when you delete or guard a handler; stale entries fail too.
Run the test after every handler change.

## Style that ruff does not catch

- German UI strings, including toasts: `rx.toast.error("Fehler beim Erstellen der
  Abteilung.", position="top-right")`. English for code, comments, docstrings, logs.
- `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` per module; `%s` arguments, never f-strings
  in log calls; `logger.exception(...)` in the final `except Exception` of a handler.
- Handler error shape: `ValidationError` → German hint, `IntegrityError` → duplicate
  message, `Exception` → `logger.exception` plus a generic German error toast.
- Colors, radii and shadows only from `alloq_commons.theme` (`theme.CARD`,
  `theme.TEXT_MUTED`, `theme.BLUE[6]`, ...). The theme is macOS blue; ignore the old
  teal design artifact.
- Use `mn.*` components. Load `appkit-mantine-reference` before using one you have
  not used in this task; its props are not in your training data.
- HTML attributes on `mn` inputs: `max_length=20` turns into CSS and limits nothing.
  Use `custom_attrs={"maxLength": 20}` for the browser limit, and keep the real check
  in the write model (`Field(max_length=20)`).
- State vars: `name: rx.Field[T] = rx.field(default)`; lists use
  `rx.field(default_factory=list)`. Type hints on every function, including tests.
- Prefer shared parts over new ones: `modal_form_layout`, `modal_footer`,
  `delete_dialog`, `toolbar_search`, `primary_button`, `section`, `app_page`,
  `window_toolbar`, `de_number`.

## Testing standards

Coverage must stay at 80 % or more (branch coverage, `fail_under = 80`). Put tests in
the package that owns the code: `components/<pkg>/tests/test_<feature>.py`. App-level
tests and the guards live in `tests/`.

- **Entity/model**: `to_dict()` keys, `XCreate` rejects bad input.
- **Service**: plain unit tests with hand-built inputs, no mocks needed.
- **State**: create the state directly, patch `MODULE.x_repo` and
  `MODULE.get_asyncdb_session`, fake the admin with `_as_admin`, and drive handlers
  with `_run`, which returns the toast text. Copy the helpers from
  `components/alloq-commons/tests/test_departments.py`.
- **Component**: render with `str(component())` and assert on var names or module
  constants. `str()` escapes umlauts (`ä` becomes `\u00e4`), so assert on the constant.
- **Migration with data changes**: add a test in `tests/test_migrations.py` that runs
  the migration offline on SQLite.

Recipes and snippets: `references/testing.md`.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Test written first; new behaviour and the bug case are covered
- [ ] `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test` all green
- [ ] `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` and `tests/test_component_boundaries.py` green
- [ ] Every new handler has its guard or its allowlist entry
- [ ] New migration is hand-written, uses `op.batch_alter_table` for column changes,
      has a real `downgrade()`, and its revision is added to `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in
      `app/desktop/schema.py`
- [ ] No touched file grew past 1000 lines; files already over it did not grow
      without reason (see `references/pitfalls.md`)
- [ ] German UI text, theme tokens, no `print`, no f-strings in logs
- [ ] Memory updated with new traps or decisions

Per change type (new field, new handler, new page, new service, bug fix):
`references/checklists.md`. Known traps: `references/pitfalls.md`.

## Which generic skill for what

| Need | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| Python style, logging, typing, design patterns | `python-coding`, `python-clean-code` |
| Reflex state design, events, background tasks | `reflex-state-and-architecture`, `reflex-docs` |
| Writing state tests in general | `reflex-testing-state` |
| Config, service registry, repositories, column types | `appkit-commons` |
| Any `mn.*` component or prop | `appkit-mantine-reference` |
| Shrinking a big file you touched | `code-cleanup` |

import each other unless that import already exists. `app` may import everything.

`alloq_commons` has both `state/` (departments, roles) and `states/` (holidays). Put
new code next to its closest neighbour and do not merge the folders unasked.

Details, snippets and the background-load pattern: `references/architecture.md`.

## Where does this code belong?

- **Pure calculation** (scores, sums, sorting, grouping, labels) goes into a service
  function or a small dataclass, testable without a database. Examples:
  `alloq_dashboard/services/resource_path.py`, `alloq_project/services/project_sorting.py`.
- **Database reads and writes** go through a repository method, or a loader function
  such as `load_departments()` or `portfolio_inputs.py`. States do not build SQL.
- **UI state** (open dialogs, filters, toggles, selection) lives in the state. When the
  state file is large, put new vars and handlers into a mixin
  (`class XListState(rx.State, mixin=True)`), never into a substate; substates break
  tests that create the state on its own.
- **Rendering** goes into function components that read state vars. No logic beyond
  `rx.cond` / `rx.foreach` and formatting.
- **A value both the UI and a test need** (labels, messages, column lists) becomes a
  module constant, so tests can assert on it.

## Security: the handler authorization contract

Access levels (`alloq_commons.access`): admins may do everything; the project
manager role may read and edit every planning page (dashboard, planning, projects,
team) but not the administration; the employee role may only read planning and
projects. Page guards (`admin_only=True`, `editor_only`, `viewer_only`) only hide
the page. Event handlers run over the websocket for anyone with a session, so every
handler protects itself. `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` enforces this for all
states in the four packages. For each new or changed handler pick exactly one case:

1. **Reads or writes data in a planning package** (`alloq_dashboard`,
   `alloq_project`, `alloq_team`, `SidebarState`) → `@rx.event` then
   `@requires_editor` from `alloq_commons.access`. This is the default; the guard
   test rejects `@requires_admin` there.
1b. **Administration state** (`DepartmentState`, `RoleState`, `HolidayState`,
   `DatabaseAccessState`, listed in `ADMIN_STATES`) → `@requires_admin` from
   `appkit_user.authentication.decorators`.
2. **Read-only load the employee role may also run** → `@requires_viewer` from
   `alloq_commons.access`, and add the name to `VIEWER_HANDLERS`. It must not write.
3. **Only changes UI state** (open/close, set filter, toggle) → no decorator, add the
   name to `UI_ONLY_HANDLERS["<ConcreteState>"]`. The test scans its source and the
   `self.` helpers it calls for DB markers (`get_asyncdb_session`, `_repo.`,
   `aggregation.`, ...), so a UI-only handler must not touch a repository or session.
4. **Background handler** (`@rx.event(background=True)`) → guard decorators are not
   allowed (they need the state lock). Check edit rights inside `async with self`
   through `_CardLoadMixin._run_card_load` (`_can_edit`) and list it in
   `INLINE_ADMIN_CHECK`.

Edit controls in the planning UI go inside `editor_only(...)` or use
`disabled=~CAN_EDIT`; `admin_only(...)` is for administration only.

Handlers defined in a mixin are listed under the concrete state that mixes it in
(`TeamState`, `ProjectState`, `PlanningStore`), because the test skips mixins.
Remove allowlist entries when you delete or guard a handler; stale entries fail too.
Run the test after every handler change.

## Style that ruff does not catch

- German UI strings, including toasts: `rx.toast.error("Fehler beim Erstellen der
  Abteilung.", position="top-right")`. English for code, comments, docstrings, logs.
- `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` per module; `%s` arguments, never f-strings
  in log calls; `logger.exception(...)` in the final `except Exception` of a handler.
- Handler error shape: `ValidationError` → German hint, `IntegrityError` → duplicate
  message, `Exception` → `logger.exception` plus a generic German error toast.
- Colors, radii and shadows only from `alloq_commons.theme` (`theme.CARD`,
  `theme.TEXT_MUTED`, `theme.BLUE[6]`, ...). The theme is macOS blue; ignore the old
  teal design artifact.
- Use `mn.*` components. Load `appkit-mantine-reference` before using one you have
  not used in this task; its props are not in your training data.
- HTML attributes on `mn` inputs: `max_length=20` turns into CSS and limits nothing.
  Use `custom_attrs={"maxLength": 20}` for the browser limit, and keep the real check
  in the write model (`Field(max_length=20)`).
- State vars: `name: rx.Field[T] = rx.field(default)`; lists use
  `rx.field(default_factory=list)`. Type hints on every function, including tests.
- Prefer shared parts over new ones: `modal_form_layout`, `modal_footer`,
  `delete_dialog`, `toolbar_search`, `primary_button`, `section`, `app_page`,
  `window_toolbar`, `de_number`.

## Testing standards

Coverage must stay at 80 % or more (branch coverage, `fail_under = 80`). Put tests in
the package that owns the code: `components/<pkg>/tests/test_<feature>.py`. App-level
tests and the guards live in `tests/`.

- **Entity/model**: `to_dict()` keys, `XCreate` rejects bad input.
- **Service**: plain unit tests with hand-built inputs, no mocks needed.
- **State**: create the state directly, patch `MODULE.x_repo` and
  `MODULE.get_asyncdb_session`, fake the admin with `_as_admin`, and drive handlers
  with `_run`, which returns the toast text. Copy the helpers from
  `components/alloq-commons/tests/test_departments.py`.
- **Component**: render with `str(component())` and assert on var names or module
  constants. `str()` escapes umlauts (`ä` becomes `\u00e4`), so assert on the constant.
- **Migration with data changes**: add a test in `tests/test_migrations.py` that runs
  the migration offline on SQLite.

Recipes and snippets: `references/testing.md`.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Test written first; new behaviour and the bug case are covered
- [ ] `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test` all green
- [ ] `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` and `tests/test_component_boundaries.py` green
- [ ] Every new handler has its guard or its allowlist entry
- [ ] New migration is hand-written, uses `op.batch_alter_table` for column changes,
      has a real `downgrade()`, and its revision is added to `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in
      `app/desktop/schema.py`
- [ ] No touched file grew past 1000 lines; files already over it did not grow
      without reason (see `references/pitfalls.md`)
- [ ] German UI text, theme tokens, no `print`, no f-strings in logs
- [ ] Memory updated with new traps or decisions

Per change type (new field, new handler, new page, new service, bug fix):
`references/checklists.md`. Known traps: `references/pitfalls.md`.

## Which generic skill for what

| Need | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| Python style, logging, typing, design patterns | `python-coding`, `python-clean-code` |
| Reflex state design, events, background tasks | `reflex-state-and-architecture`, `reflex-docs` |
| Writing state tests in general | `reflex-testing-state` |
| Config, service registry, repositories, column types | `appkit-commons` |
| Any `mn.*` component or prop | `appkit-mantine-reference` |
| Shrinking a big file you touched | `code-cleanup` |

import reflex as rx
from alloq_commons.access import no_access, viewer_only
from alloq_commons.components.shell import app_page
from alloq_commons.components.toolbar import scope_bar, window_toolbar

import appkit_mantine as mn
from alloq_project.components.planning_filter_row import (
    absence_filter_row,
    planning_filter_row,
    planning_view_switch,
)
from alloq_project.components.planning_gantt import planning_gantt
from alloq_project.components.planning_grid import planning_grid
from alloq_project.components.planning_project_view import (
    planning_project_view,
)
from alloq_project.components.planning_toolbar import planning_toolbar
from alloq_project.components.project_overview import project_overview
from alloq_project.components.project_plan_modal import project_plan_modal
from alloq_project.components.project_toolbar import project_filter, project_toolbar
from alloq_project.states.planning_grid_state import PlanningStore
from alloq_project.states.project_state import ProjectState


def create_planning_page(
    sidebar: rx.Component,
    route: str = "/plan",
    title: str = "Ressourcenplanung",
) -> rx.Component:

    @app_page(
        route=route,
        title=title,
        sidebar=sidebar,
        toolbar=window_toolbar(
            "Ressourcenplanung",
            rx.cond(
                PlanningStore.view_mode == "Abwesenheiten",
                "Abwesenheiten und Besetzung je Woche",
                "Kapazität und Zuweisungen je Woche",
            ),
            center=planning_view_switch(),
            actions=planning_toolbar(),
        ),
        scope=scope_bar(
            rx.cond(
                PlanningStore.view_mode == "Abwesenheiten",
                absence_filter_row(),
                planning_filter_row(),
            )
        ),
        padded=False,
        on_load=PlanningStore.load,
    )
    def _planning_page() -> rx.Component:
        return viewer_only(
            mn.box(
                rx.match(
                    PlanningStore.view_mode,
                    ("Grid", planning_grid()),
                    ("Abwesenheiten", planning_gantt()),
                    ("Projekte", planning_project_view()),
                    rx.fragment(),
                ),
                project_plan_modal(),
                class_name="aq-planning-body",
            ),
            fallback=no_access(),
        )

    return _planning_page


def create_projects_overview_page(
    sidebar: rx.Component,
    route: str = "/projects",
    title: str = "Projekte",
) -> rx.Component:

    @app_page(
        route=route,
        title=title,
        sidebar=sidebar,
        toolbar=window_toolbar(
            "Projekte",
            ProjectState.subtitle,
            center=project_filter(),
            actions=project_toolbar(),
        ),
        padded=False,
        on_load=[ProjectState.load_projects],
    )
    def _projects_overview_page() -> rx.Component:
        return viewer_only(project_overview(), fallback=no_access())

    return _projects_overview_page
import reflex as rx
from alloq_commons.access import CAN_EDIT, editor_only
from alloq_commons.components.modal_layout import DRAWER_CLASS, MODAL_CLASS
from alloq_commons.models.project import Project
from alloq_commons.models.view_mode import VIEW_MODE_GRID
from alloq_project.components.project_card import project_card
from alloq_project.components.project_form import (
    form_footer,
    form_layout,
    project_form_fields,
)
from alloq_project.components.project_resource_tab import ressourcen_tab
from alloq_project.components.project_risk_tab import risiken_tab
from alloq_project.components.project_status_tab import status_tab
from alloq_project.components.project_table import project_table
from alloq_project.states.project_state import ProjectState, ProjectValidationState
from reflex.vars import ArrayVar

import appkit_mantine as mn


def add_project_modal() -> rx.Component:
    """Modal for creating a new project."""
    return mn.modal(
        form_layout(
            content=mn.flex(
                project_form_fields(),
                mn.space(height="1.5rem"),
                direction="column",
                width="100%",
                key=ProjectValidationState.form_version.to(str),
            ),
            footer=form_footer(
                "Projekt speichern",
                ProjectState.close_add_modal,
                disabled=ProjectValidationState.is_form_invalid,
            ),
            on_submit=ProjectState.create_project,
        ),
        title="Neues Projekt",
        opened=ProjectState.add_modal_open,
        on_close=ProjectState.close_add_modal,
        size="lg",
        centered=True,
        class_name=MODAL_CLASS,
        overlay_props={"backgroundOpacity": 0.5, "blur": 4},
    )


READ_ONLY_FIELDSET = {"display": "contents"}
"""Keeps the drawer layout: the tabs stay direct children of the flex column."""


def project_detail_drawer() -> rx.Component:
    """Right-side drawer with Status, Ressourcen, Risiken, Daten tabs."""
    return mn.drawer(
        rx.flex(
            rx.box(
                mn.segmented_control(
                    data=[
                        {"value": "status", "label": "Status"},
                        {"value": "ressourcen", "label": "Ressourcen"},
                        {"value": "risiken", "label": "Risiken"},
                        {"value": "daten", "label": "Daten"},
                    ],
                    value=ProjectState.active_tab,
                    on_change=ProjectState.set_active_tab,
                    full_width=True,
                    size="sm",
                    color="blue",
                    radius="md",
                    bg="var(--alloq-surface-solid)",
                    style={"flexShrink": "0"},
                    w="66%",
                ),
                padding="9px 18px",
                background="var(--alloq-surface-muted)",
                box_shadow="0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08)",
                z_index="1",
                width="100%",
                flex_shrink="0",
            ),
            # A disabled fieldset turns every input and button read-only.
            rx.el.fieldset(
                rx.match(
                    ProjectState.active_tab,
                    (
                        "daten",
                        form_layout(
                            content=mn.flex(
                                project_form_fields(),
                                mn.space(height="1.5rem"),
                                direction="column",
                                width="100%",
                                key=ProjectValidationState.form_version.to(str),
                            ),
                            footer=editor_only(
                                form_footer(
                                    "Projekt aktualisieren",
                                    ProjectState.close_detail_drawer,
                                    disabled=ProjectValidationState.is_form_invalid,
                                )
                            ),
                            on_submit=ProjectState.update_project,
                        ),
                    ),
                    ("status", status_tab()),
                    ("ressourcen", ressourcen_tab()),
                    risiken_tab(),
                ),
                disabled=~CAN_EDIT,
                style=READ_ONLY_FIELDSET,
            ),
            direction="column",
            gap="md",
            height="100%",
            width="100%",

def _today() -> date:

def status_tone(state: str) -> str:
    return STATUS_TONES.get(state, "neutral")


def _matches(project: Project, list_filter: str) -> bool:
    if list_filter in (FILTER_ALL, FILTER_MINE):
        return True
    return project.state == list_filter


def _is_closed(project: Project) -> bool:
    return project.state == ProjectStateEnum.COMPLETED


def _is_planned(project: Project) -> bool:
    return project.state == ProjectStateEnum.PLANNED


def _is_internal(project: Project) -> bool:
    return project.is_internal and not (_is_closed(project) or _is_planned(project))


def _is_regular(project: Project) -> bool:
    return not (_is_closed(project) or _is_internal(project) or _is_planned(project))

    @rx.var
    def show_inspector(self) -> bool:
        return self.inspector_open == "1"

    def _rows_where(self, predicate: Callable[[Project], bool]) -> list[Project]:
        """Visible projects of any owner, respecting the "Meine" filter."""

            self.my_projects
            if self.list_filter == FILTER_MINE
            else self.filtered_projects
        )
        return [p for p in source if predicate(p) and _matches(p, self.list_filter)]

    def mine_rows(self) -> list[Project]:
        return [
            p
            for p in self.my_projects
            if _is_regular(p) and _matches(p, self.list_filter)
        ]

def status_tone(state: str) -> str:

def _matches(project: Project, list_filter: str) -> bool:
    if list_filter in (FILTER_ALL, FILTER_MINE):

    return project.state == list_filter


def _is_closed(project: Project) -> bool:
    return project.state == ProjectStateEnum.COMPLETED


def _is_planned(project: Project) -> bool:
    return project.state == ProjectStateEnum.PLANNED


def _is_internal(project: Project) -> bool:
    return project.is_internal and not (_is_closed(project) or _is_planned(project))

    return not (_is_closed(project) or _is_internal(project) or _is_planned(project))

        ]

"""Architecture guard: component packages must not import the host app."""

import ast
from pathlib import Path

COMPONENTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "components"


def _imports_host_app(path: Path) -> bool:
    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module:
            names = [node.module]
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            names = [alias.name for alias in node.names]
        else:
            continue
        if any(name == "app" or name.startswith("app.") for name in names):
            return True
    return False


def test_components_do_not_import_host_app() -> None:
    offenders = [
        str(path.relative_to(COMPONENTS))
        for path in COMPONENTS.glob("*/src/**/*.py")
        if _imports_host_app(path)
    ]
    assert offenders == []


def test_app_roles_reexports_commons_roles() -> None:

"""Architecture guard: component packages must not import the host app."""

import ast
from pathlib import Path

COMPONENTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "components"


def _imports_host_app(path: Path) -> bool:
    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module:
            names = [node.module]
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            names = [alias.name for alias in node.names]
        else:
            continue
        if any(name == "app" or name.startswith("app.") for name in names):
            return True
    return False


def test_components_do_not_import_host_app() -> None:
    offenders = [
        str(path.relative_to(COMPONENTS))
        for path in COMPONENTS.glob("*/src/**/*.py")
        if _imports_host_app(path)
    ]
    assert offenders == []

"""Permission roles of the alloq application (shared by app and components)."""

from alloq_commons.models.department import Department
from appkit_commons.roles import Role

PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE = Role(
    id=1,
    name="project_manager",
    label="Projektmanager",
    description="Voller Zugriff auf Planung, Projekte und Team, ohne Administration",
)

EMPLOYEE_ROLE = Role(
    id=2,
    name="employee",
    label="Mitarbeiter",
    description="Lesezugriff auf Projekte und Ressourcenplanung",
)


ALL_ROLES: list[Role] = [
    PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE,
    EMPLOYEE_ROLE,
]

DEPARTMENT_ROLE_GROUP = "Abteilungen"


def department_role_name(department_id: int) -> str:
    """Permission role name of a department; keyed by id so renames keep it."""
    return f"department_{department_id}"


def department_roles(departments: list[Department]) -> list[Role]:
    """Permission roles offered in user management, one per department."""
    return [
        Role(
            name=department_role_name(d.id),
            label=d.label,
            description=f"Mitglied der Abteilung {d.name}",
            group=DEPARTMENT_ROLE_GROUP,
        )
        for d in departments
    ]
"""Access levels of the alloq roles next to appkit's admin rights.

Admins may do everything. Project managers may read and edit every planning
page; the administration pages stay admin-only (``@requires_admin``). Users
with the employee role may only read the projects and planning pages.
"""

import inspect
import logging
from collections.abc import Callable
from functools import wraps
from typing import Any, Final

import reflex as rx

import appkit_mantine as mn
from alloq_commons.roles import EMPLOYEE_ROLE, PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE
from appkit_user.authentication.backend.models import User
from appkit_user.authentication.states import LoginState, UserSession

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_NOT_AUTHORIZED_MSG: Final = "Sie haben keine Berechtigung für diese Aktion."

ACCESS_LEVEL_ATTR: Final = "alloq_access_level"
"""Attribute naming the guard (``viewer``/``editor``) of a decorated handler."""

IS_ADMIN: Final = UserSession.user.is_admin
"""Frontend Var: the signed-in user is an admin."""
CAN_EDIT: Final = IS_ADMIN | UserSession.user.roles.contains(PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE.name)
"""Frontend Var: the signed-in user may read and edit the planning pages."""
CAN_VIEW: Final = CAN_EDIT | UserSession.user.roles.contains(EMPLOYEE_ROLE.name)
"""Frontend Var: the signed-in user may read projects and planning."""


def can_edit(user: User) -> bool:
    """Whether ``user`` may read and edit the planning pages."""
    return user.is_admin or PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE.name in user.roles


def can_view(user: User) -> bool:
    """Whether ``user`` may read the projects and planning pages."""
    return can_edit(user) or EMPLOYEE_ROLE.name in user.roles


NO_ACCESS_MSG: Final = (
    "Sie haben nicht die notwendigen Berechtigungen, um auf diese Seite zuzugreifen."
)


def no_access() -> rx.Component:
    """Page content for signed-in users without read access."""
    return mn.center(mn.text(NO_ACCESS_MSG, fz="15px", fw=500), h="60vh", px=24)


def viewer_only(*children: Any, fallback: rx.Component | None = None) -> rx.Component:
    """Render ``children`` for admins, project managers and employees."""
    return rx.cond(CAN_VIEW, rx.fragment(*children), fallback)


def editor_only(*children: Any, fallback: rx.Component | None = None) -> rx.Component:
    """Render ``children`` for admins and project managers (edit controls)."""
    return rx.cond(CAN_EDIT, rx.fragment(*children), fallback)


def admin_only(*children: Any, fallback: rx.Component | None = None) -> rx.Component:
    """Render ``children`` for admins only (administration)."""
    return rx.cond(IS_ADMIN, rx.fragment(*children), fallback)


def _guard[F: Callable[..., Any]](
    func: F, allowed: Callable[[User], bool], level: str
) -> F:
    """Wrap event handler ``func`` so only users passing ``allowed`` run it.

    Mirrors appkit's ``requires_admin``: unauthenticated callers are redirected
    to login, everyone else without the right gets a permission error.
    """

    async def _check(self: Any) -> tuple[bool, Any]:
        """``(allowed, event)``; ``event`` answers a denied call."""
        login_state = await self.get_state(LoginState)
        user = await login_state.authenticated_user
        if user is None:
            logger.debug("User not authenticated, redirecting to login.")
            return False, await login_state.redir()
        if not allowed(user):
            logger.warning(
                "User user_id=%s denied %s action '%s'",
                user.user_id,
                level,
                func.__name__,
            )
            return False, rx.toast.error(_NOT_AUTHORIZED_MSG, position="top-right")
        return True, None

    @wraps(func)
    async def async_gen_wrapper(self: Any, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        ok, event = await _check(self)
        if not ok:
            yield event
            return
        async for item in func(self, *args, **kwargs):
            yield item

    @wraps(func)
    async def async_wrapper(self: Any, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        ok, event = await _check(self)
        if not ok:
            return event
        return await func(self, *args, **kwargs)

    wrapper = async_gen_wrapper if inspect.isasyncgenfunction(func) else async_wrapper
    setattr(wrapper, ACCESS_LEVEL_ATTR, level)
    return wrapper  # type: ignore[return-value]


def requires_viewer[F: Callable[..., Any]](func: F) -> F:
    """Allow a read-only event for admins, project managers and employees."""
    return _guard(func, can_view, "viewer")


def requires_editor[F: Callable[..., Any]](func: F) -> F:
    """Allow a reading or writing event for admins and project managers."""
    return _guard(func, can_edit, "editor")
from alloq_commons.roles import ALL_ROLES, PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE

__all__ = ["ALL_ROLES", "PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE"]

# Refined prompt: "Angebote" page as new package `alloq-offer`

> Load `alloq-implementation` first, then `appkit-mantine-reference` before using any `mn.*` component you have not used in this task. Follow the test-first workflow and definition of done from that skill.

## Task

Add a new page **Angebote** (`/offers`) that lists offers calculated for customer projects. It looks and behaves like the Projekte list view: a macOS-style table with status groups, a toolbar with search, filter segments and a "Angebot anlegen" button, and an inspector on the right that shows the clicked offer. Offers can be created and edited, but never deleted; they can be archived and restored.

The feature lives in a **new, independent uv workspace package `components/alloq-offer`** (import name `alloq_offer`). Entity, model, repository, services, states, components and the page factory all live in this package. It depends only on `alloq-commons` and appkit, never on `alloq-project`, `alloq-team`, `alloq-dashboard` or `app`.

Access is controlled by a **new permission role `offer_editor`** (label "Angebote"). Admins, project managers and users with `offer_editor` may see and edit offers. Nobody else sees the page or its sidebar entry.

## Context (found in the repo)

- Reference slice to copy the shape from: the Projekte list view.
  - Page factory: `components/alloq-project/src/alloq_project/pages.py` → `create_projects_overview_page` (uses `app_page`, `window_toolbar`, `viewer_only(..., fallback=no_access())`).
  - Table: `alloq_project/components/project_table.py` (`TEMPLATE`, `COLUMNS`, `_row`, `_group`, `split_view`, `list_header`, `list_row`, `cell_main`, `badge`, `number`, `empty_list`).
  - Inspector: `alloq_project/components/project_inspector.py` (`inspector`, `inspector_section`, `key_values`, `plain_button`, inline `mn.select` for status, inline `mn.date_input` with "Heute" action icon, copy-to-clipboard action icon in `_booking_number`).
  - Toolbar: `alloq_project/components/project_toolbar.py` (`segmented`, `toolbar_search`, `icon_button("panel-right", ...)`, `primary_button`).
  - List state mixin: `alloq_project/states/project_list_state.py` (`FILTERS`, `STATUS_TONES`, `inspected_id`, `inspector_open` as `rx.LocalStorage`, `show_inspector`, grouped row computed vars).
  - Create modal: `add_project_modal` in `alloq_project/components/project_overview.py`; shared parts `modal_form_layout`, `modal_footer` in `alloq_commons/components/modal_layout.py`.
- Shared UI parts: `alloq_commons/components/list_view.py`, `toolbar.py`, `formatters.py` (`de_number`), `shell.py` (`app_page`). Colors only from `alloq_commons.theme`.
- Entity/repo pattern: `alloq_commons/entities/department.py`, `alloq_commons/repositories/department_repository.py` (`BaseRepository[XEntity, AsyncSession]`, module singleton). Money columns use `Numeric` + `Decimal` like `alloq_commons/entities/price_list.py`. Enum-as-German-label pattern: `ProjectStateEnum(enum.StrEnum)` in `alloq_commons/entities/project.py`.
- Package template: `components/alloq-team/pyproject.toml` and its `src/alloq_team/{components,services,states,pages.py}` + `tests/` layout.
- Roles and access: `alloq_commons/roles.py` (`PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE` id 1, `EMPLOYEE_ROLE` id 2, `ALL_ROLES`), `alloq_commons/access.py` (`CAN_EDIT`, `editor_only`, `_guard`, `requires_editor`, `ACCESS_LEVEL_ATTR`). The word "editor" is already used there for admin + project manager, so the new role is named `offer_editor`.
- Sidebar: `app/components/sidebar.py` (`PLANNING_ITEMS`, `VIEWER_ROUTES`, `_guarded_nav_item`). Registration: `app/app.py`.
- Guards: `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` (`PACKAGES`, `EDITOR_PACKAGES`, `UI_ONLY_HANDLERS`, access-level checks), `tests/test_component_boundaries.py`.
- Migrations: current head is `bd91ef12ac34` (`alembic/versions/2026_10_19_department_highlight.py`); `alembic/env.py` imports `alloq_commons.entities` to register tables; new revisions go first in `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in `app/desktop/schema.py`.
- Root `pyproject.toml` lists every package in `dependencies`, `[tool.uv.sources]`, `[[tool.bumpversion.files]]`, pytest `testpaths` and coverage `source`.

## Requirements

### 1. Package scaffold
1. Create `components/alloq-offer/pyproject.toml` (copy `alloq-team`, name `alloq-offer`, same version, dependency `alloq-commons`, wheel package `src/alloq_offer`).
2. Layout: `src/alloq_offer/{__init__.py, entities.py, models.py, repository.py, services/, states/, components/, pages.py}` and `tests/`. Split into sub-modules only if a file grows large.
3. Register in root `pyproject.toml`: `dependencies`, `[tool.uv.sources]`, a `[[tool.bumpversion.files]]` block, `testpaths`, coverage `source`. Run `uv sync` (via `task sync`).

### 2. Data layer (in `alloq_offer`)
4. Enums (`enum.StrEnum`, values are the German labels shown in the UI):
   - `OfferStateEnum`: `NEW = "Neu"`, `IN_PROGRESS = "In Bearbeitung"`, `SENT = "Versendet"`.
   - `CustomerIndustryUnit`: values are the codes `CP, FS, U, P, H, IMC`, plus a module constant `CIU_LABELS` mapping code → label: "Consumer Services - CP", "Financial Services - FS", "Utilities - U", "Public - P", "Health - H", "Industrial Midcaps - IMC".
5. `OfferEntity(Entity, Base)`, table `offers`:
   | Column | Type | Rule |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | `title` | String(255) | required |
   | `customer` | String(255) | required |
   | `person_days` | Numeric(8,2) | required, ≥ 0 ("PT") |
   | `risk_buffer_days` | Numeric(8,2) | required, ≥ 0, default 0 ("Risikopuffer (PT)") |
   | `production_cost` | Numeric(12,2) | required, ≥ 0 ("Herstellkosten (HK)", €) |
   | `recommended_price` | Numeric(12,2) | required, ≥ 0 ("Empfohlener VK", €) |
   | `key_accounter` | String(255) | required, free text |
   | `ciu` | String(10) | required, one of the CIU codes |
   | `sharepoint_url` | String(2048) | optional |
   | `sent_date` | Date | optional |
   | `state` | String(20) | required, default `Neu` |
   | `archived` | Boolean | not null, default false, `server_default=false()` |
   `to_dict()` returns every field plus `id`, `created`, `updated`.
6. Pydantic `Offer` read model and `OfferCreate` write model with `Field` limits matching the columns; `sharepoint_url` must be empty or start with `http://` or `https://`; `ciu` and `state` validated against the enums; strings stripped and non-empty where required.
7. `OfferRepository(BaseRepository[OfferEntity, AsyncSession])` with `find_all_ordered()` (newest `updated` first) and module singleton `offer_repo`. No delete method is used anywhere.
8. Make the table known to Alembic: `alloq_offer` must register `OfferEntity` on `Base.metadata`, and `alembic/env.py` imports `alloq_offer.entities` next to `alloq_commons.entities`. Make sure the SQLite test setup also sees the table.
9. Hand-written migration `alembic/versions/2026_10_21_offers.py`: new revision id, `down_revision = "bd91ef12ac34"`, `op.create_table("offers", ...)` with all columns and an index on `state`; real `downgrade()` dropping the table. Add the revision as first entry of `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in `app/desktop/schema.py`.

### 3. Pure services (`alloq_offer/services/`)
10. `apply_state_change(state: str, sent_date: date | None, new_state: str, today: date) -> date | None`: when `new_state` is `Versendet` and `sent_date` is empty, return `today`; otherwise return `sent_date` unchanged (moving back to Neu/In Bearbeitung keeps the date). Used by create, edit and the inline status select.
11. Derived values for the inspector: `total_days = person_days + risk_buffer_days`, `margin_pct = (recommended_price - production_cost) / recommended_price * 100` (None when VK is 0). Plain functions, unit-tested.
12. Filtering/grouping helpers: search over title, customer and key accounter (case-insensitive); filter segments; sort by column.

### 4. Roles and access (small, shared touchpoints in `alloq_commons`)
13. `alloq_commons/roles.py`: add `OFFER_EDITOR_ROLE = Role(id=3, name="offer_editor", label="Angebote", description="Lesen und Bearbeiten der Angebote")` and append it to `ALL_ROLES` so it appears in user management.
14. `alloq_commons/access.py`: add `CAN_EDIT_OFFERS` (frontend Var: `CAN_EDIT | roles.contains("offer_editor")`), `can_edit_offers(user)`, `offers_only(*children, fallback=None)` and `requires_offer_editor` built on the existing `_guard` with access level `"offer_editor"`. Do not change the meaning of the existing levels: an `offer_editor`-only user gets no planning, projects or team access.
15. Every data handler in `alloq_offer` states uses `@rx.event` + `@requires_offer_editor`; UI-only handlers (open/close modal, set filter, search, inspect, toggle inspector) have no decorator and are listed in `UI_ONLY_HANDLERS["OfferState"]`.
16. `tests/test_handler_authorization.py`: add `"alloq_offer"` to `PACKAGES`; add an `OFFER_PACKAGES = {"alloq_offer"}` rule so handlers there must carry the `offer_editor` level (and treat that level as guarded); add a test that offer handlers are not `requires_admin`/`requires_editor`. Keep all existing tests green.

### 5. State (`alloq_offer/states/offer_state.py`)
17. `OfferState(rx.State)` with `offers`, `is_loading`, `search_filter`, `list_filter`, `sort_column`, `sort_desc`, `inspected_id`, `inspector_open` (`rx.LocalStorage("1", name="alloq_offers_inspector")`), `form_open`, `editing_id` (0 = create), and form draft fields. If the file nears ~400 lines, move list logic into a mixin (`rx.State, mixin=True`), never a substate.
18. Handlers: `load_offers`, `create_offer(form_data)`, `update_offer(form_data)`, `update_inspected_state(offer_id, state)` (applies requirement 10 and saves), `set_inspected_sent_date(offer_id, value)` + save on blur, `set_sent_date_today(offer_id)`, `archive_offer(offer_id)`, `restore_offer(offer_id)`. Error shape per skill: `ValidationError` → German hint toast, `Exception` → `logger.exception` + generic German error toast. Success toasts in German.
19. Computed vars: grouped rows `new_rows`, `in_progress_rows`, `sent_rows`, `archived_rows`; `inspected` offer; `row_count`; totals for the footer.

### 6. UI (`alloq_offer/components/`)
20. **Toolbar** (`window_toolbar("Angebote", subtitle, center=filter, actions=...)`): filter segments `Alle`, `Neu`, `In Bearbeitung`, `Versendet`, `Archiviert`; `toolbar_search` placeholder "Angebot, Kunde oder Key Accounter"; inspector toggle `icon_button("panel-right", ...)`; `offers_only(primary_button("Angebot anlegen", "plus", ...))`. No grid/card view toggle (list only).
21. **Table** (`split_view` with inspector): columns `Angebot` (title + customer via `cell_main`), `CIU` (badge with code), `Status` (badge, tones: Neu → info, In Bearbeitung → warning/accent, Versendet → positive), `PT` (person days + buffer, `de_number`), `HK` (€), `VK` (€), `Versendet am` (DD.MM.YYYY or "–"). Groups: Neu, In Bearbeitung, Versendet; archived offers are hidden except under the `Archiviert` filter, where they form one group. Footer row with sums of PT, HK and VK. Sortable headers. Click selects into the inspector; double click opens the edit modal. Empty state "Keine Angebote mit diesem Filter." / "Noch keine Angebote vorhanden."
22. **Create/edit modal** (`mn.modal` + `modal_form_layout`/`modal_footer`), title "Neues Angebot" / "Angebot bearbeiten". Fields, German labels:
    - Angebotstitel (text, required)
    - Kunde (text, required)
    - Kalkulierte Personentage (PT) (number, ≥ 0, 2 decimals)
    - Risikopuffer (PT) (number, ≥ 0, default 0)
    - Herstellkosten (HK) (number, €, ≥ 0)
    - Empfohlener VK (number, €, ≥ 0)
    - Key Accounter (text, required)
    - CIU (`mn.select` with the six labels, required)
    - SharePoint-Link (URL text input, optional)
    - Versendet am (`mn.date_input`, `locale="de"`, `value_format="DD.MM.YYYY"`, clearable)
    - Status (`mn.select`: Neu, In Bearbeitung, Versendet; default Neu)
    Use `custom_attrs={"maxLength": N}` for text limits (not `max_length`). Save button disabled while required fields are empty. Key the uncontrolled inputs by a form version so reopening resets them.
23. **Inspector** (`inspector(..., label="Angebotsdetails")`), shown for the selected row, "Kein Angebot ausgewählt." otherwise:
    - Heading: title, customer, status badge; "Archiviert" tag when archived.
    - Actions (inside `offers_only`): "Bearbeiten" (opens edit modal), "Archivieren" / "Wiederherstellen".
    - Section "Eckdaten" (`key_values`): Status as inline `mn.select` (applies requirement 10), Versendet am as inline `mn.date_input` with a "Heute" action icon, saved on blur (copy `_date_input` from the project inspector), CIU label, Key Accounter, SharePoint link as an anchor opening in a new tab plus a copy action icon ("–" when empty).
    - Section "Kalkulation": PT, Risikopuffer, Gesamt-PT, HK, Empfohlener VK, Marge in % (from requirement 11).
    - Controls disabled via `disabled=~CAN_EDIT_OFFERS`.

### 7. Page, sidebar, registration
24. `alloq_offer/pages.py`: `create_offers_page(sidebar, route="/offers", title="Angebote")` using `app_page(..., padded=False, on_load=[OfferState.load_offers])`; body wrapped in `offers_only(..., fallback=no_access())`.
25. `app/app.py`: `create_offers_page(sidebar())`.
26. `app/components/sidebar.py`: add `("/offers", "Angebote", "file-text")` to `PLANNING_ITEMS` after Projekte; `_guarded_nav_item` uses `offers_only` for that route (e.g. a small route → guard mapping instead of the `VIEWER_ROUTES` if/else).

## Deliverables

- `components/alloq-offer/` package with `pyproject.toml`, source modules above, `tests/`.
- Edits: root `pyproject.toml`, `alembic/env.py`, `alembic/versions/2026_10_21_offers.py`, `app/desktop/schema.py`, `alloq_commons/roles.py`, `alloq_commons/access.py`, `app/app.py`, `app/components/sidebar.py`, `tests/test_handler_authorization.py`.
- Tests in `components/alloq-offer/tests/`:
  - `test_offer_model.py`: `to_dict()` keys; `OfferCreate` rejects empty title/customer, negative numbers, unknown CIU/state, non-http SharePoint URL.
  - `test_offer_services.py`: `apply_state_change` (empty date set on Versendet, existing date kept, date kept when moving back), totals, margin incl. VK = 0, search/filter/grouping/sorting.
  - `test_offer_state.py`: create, update, inline state change sets date, sent-date edit, archive/restore, filter `Archiviert`, error toasts; patch `MODULE.offer_repo` and `MODULE.get_asyncdb_session`, helpers copied from `components/alloq-commons/tests/test_departments.py`.
  - `test_offer_components.py`: render table, inspector, modal with `str(...)`; assert on module constants (umlauts are escaped).
  - Access tests in `alloq-commons` tests: `can_edit_offers` true for admin, project manager, offer_editor; false for employee and a user without roles; `can_edit` / `can_view` unchanged for an offer_editor-only user.

## Success criteria

- `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test` all green, coverage ≥ 80 %.
- `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` and `tests/test_component_boundaries.py` green; `alloq_offer` imports nothing from `app` or other feature packages.
- `uv run alembic upgrade head` then `downgrade -1` works on a fresh SQLite DB.
- `python .claude/skills/alloq-implementation/scripts/check_file_sizes.py` passes.
- Manual check on localhost: as admin, open `/offers`, create an offer, select it, change status to Versendet in the inspector and see today's date appear, change the date by hand, archive and find it under `Archiviert`, restore it. A user with only `offer_editor` sees only Angebote in the Planung section; an employee does not see Angebote.
- Memory updated with new decisions (independent package, `offer_editor` role and access level).

## Out of scope

- Deleting offers (archive only).
- Converting an offer into a project or linking offers to projects.
- Calculating PT, HK or VK from price lists or daily rates; all values are entered by hand.
- Card/grid view, export, attachments or SharePoint integration beyond storing the link.
- Sidebar badge counts for offers.
- Changing access for existing pages or roles.

    - Empfohlener VK (number, €, ≥ 0)
    - Key Accounter (text, required)

    - Section "Kalkulation": PT, Risikopuffer, Gesamt-PT, HK, Empfohlener VK, Marge in % (from requirement 11).
    - Controls disabled via `disabled=~CAN_EDIT_OFFERS`.

25. `app/app.py`: `create_offers_page(sidebar())`.

- Edits: root `pyproject.toml`, `alembic/env.py`, `alembic/versions/2026_10_21_offers.py`, `app/desktop/schema.py`, `alloq_commons/roles.py`, `alloq_commons/access.py`, `app/app.py`, `app/components/sidebar.py`, `tests/test_handler_authorization.py`.
- Tests in `components/alloq-offer/tests/`:
  - `test_offer_model.py`: `to_dict()` keys; `OfferCreate` rejects empty title/customer, negative numbers, unknown CIU/state, non-http SharePoint URL.
  - `test_offer_services.py`: `apply_state_change` (empty date set on Versendet, existing date kept, date kept when moving back), totals, margin incl. VK = 0, search/filter/grouping/sorting.
  - `test_offer_state.py`: create, update, inline state change sets date, sent-date edit, archive/restore, filter `Archiviert`, error toasts; patch `MODULE.offer_repo` and `MODULE.get_asyncdb_session`, helpers copied from `components/alloq-commons/tests/test_departments.py`.
  - `test_offer_components.py`: render table, inspector, modal with `str(...)`; assert on module constants (umlauts are escaped).
  - Access tests in `alloq-commons` tests: `can_edit_offers` true for admin, project manager, offer_editor; false for employee and a user without roles; `can_edit` / `can_view` unchanged for an offer_editor-only user.

## Success criteria

- `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test` all green, coverage ≥ 80 %.
- `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` and `tests/test_component_boundaries.py` green; `alloq_offer` imports nothing from `app` or other feature packages.
- `uv run alembic upgrade head` then `downgrade -1` works on a fresh SQLite DB.
- `python .claude/skills/alloq-implementation/scripts/check_file_sizes.py` passes.
- Manual check on localhost: as admin, open `/offers`, create an offer, select it, change status to Versendet in the inspector and see today's date appear, change the date by hand, archive and find it under `Archiviert`, restore it. A user with only `offer_editor` sees only Angebote in the Planung section; an employee does not see Angebote.
- Memory updated with new decisions (independent package, `offer_editor` role and access level).

## Out of scope

- Deleting offers (archive only).
- Converting an offer into a project or linking offers to projects.
- Calculating PT, HK or VK from price lists or daily rates; all values are entered by hand.
- Card/grid view, export, attachments or SharePoint integration beyond storing the link.
- Sidebar badge counts for offers.
- Changing access for existing pages or roles.
